title: Personal Protective Equipment (PPE)

references.label: Biosafety in Microbiological and Biomedical Laboratories (BMBL)

summary: The protective clothing and equipment worn to reduce exposure risk to laboratory personnel, chosen based on the specific hazards of the work being performed.
explanation: Standard microbiology PPE commonly includes a lab coat (closed, fastened), gloves appropriate to the task, and eye protection when there is a splash risk. PPE requirements scale with the specific risk assessment for the organism, procedure (e.g. aerosol-generating steps may require additional respiratory protection), and facility policy — there is no single fixed PPE list that applies to every laboratory task.
keyPractices: Wear a fastened lab coat dedicated to lab use, removed before leaving the lab area.
Select gloves appropriate to the specific hazard (biological vs. chemical) and change them when contaminated or torn.
Use eye/face protection for any procedure with splash or aerosol potential.
Never wear PPE (e.g. gloves) outside the lab in general areas (door handles, phones, etc.).
commonMistakes: Wearing the same gloves to touch a phone, doorknob, or personal items.
Assuming gloves alone substitute for handwashing.
